questions.title: Section A: Multiple Choice, Matching, Terminology and Correcting Statements

subQuestions.questionText:
An event where buyers come together to bid for farm produce:
A. Agricultural show
B. Co-operative farming
C. Liquidity
D. Auction
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - Auction (2 marks)
An auction is a public sale where buyers openly bid against one another and the produce is sold to the highest bidder.

subQuestions.questionText:
ONE of the following is NOT associated with the advantages of free marketing:
A. Stabilising the prices of agricultural products
B. Sales are for cash
C. Selling quality products
D. Entrepreneur shows initiative and drive
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - Stabilising the prices of agricultural products (2 marks)
Price stabilisation is a feature of controlled marketing, not free marketing. Under free marketing prices fluctuate according to supply and demand.

options.A: Stabilising the prices of agricultural products

subQuestions.questionText:
In a situation where the dairy farmer produces less cheese than the amount demanded, the price of cheese is likely to …
A. decrease.
B. remain the same.
C. increase.
D. remain constant.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - increase (2 marks)
When quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied there is a shortage, which drives the price upward.

subQuestions.questionText:
The following applies to selling:
(i) Management is profit-orientated
(ii) Short-term objective is to sell the product
(iii) Emphasis is on the product
(iv) Customer needs are neglected
Choose the CORRECT combination:
A. (i), (ii) and (iv)
B. (ii), (iii) and (iv)
C. (i), (ii) and (iii)
D. (i), (iii) and (iv)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - (ii), (iii) and (iv) (2 marks)
The selling concept focuses on the product, aims at the short-term objective of selling it, and tends to neglect customer needs. Being profit-orientated (i) describes the marketing concept, not selling.

subQuestions.questionText:
The following is NOT a problem associated with labour as a production factor:
A. Lack of training
B. Competition from industries
C. Shortage of labourers
D. Better living and working conditions
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - Better living and working conditions (2 marks)
Better living and working conditions is a positive measure that helps to retain labour, not a labour problem. The other options are all recognised labour problems.

subQuestions.questionText:
Money paid by the farmer over and above what was borrowed from the financial institution:
A. Loan
B. Interest
C. Debt
D. Capital
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - Interest (2 marks)
Interest is the extra amount, charged as a percentage of the principal, that a borrower pays a lender in addition to repaying the amount borrowed.

subQuestions.questionText:
The management principle whereby the farmer monitors production and compares the results with the expected output:
A. Control
B. Implementation
C. Planning
D. Manipulation
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - Control (2 marks)
Control is the management function of measuring actual performance against planned targets and correcting any deviations.

subQuestions.questionText:
The following statements refer to the law of diminishing returns:
(i) The addition of one unit of a production factor will not ensure a proportional increase in yield with time.
(ii) A continuous addition of inputs will initially increase the output drastically, but at a certain point the output increases at a decreasing rate.
(iii) An increase in fertiliser will result in a continuous increase in production.
(iv) With an increase in fertiliser, production will start to increase and then at a certain point it decreases with additional fertilisers.
Choose the CORRECT combination:
A. (i), (iii) and (iv)
B. (ii), (iii) and (iv)
C. (i), (ii) and (iv)
D. (i), (ii) and (iii)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - (i), (ii) and (iv) (2 marks)
The law of diminishing returns states that adding more of one input while holding others constant eventually raises output at a decreasing rate and finally reduces it. Statement (iii), a continuous increase, contradicts the law.
subQuestions.topic: Production Factors - Law of Diminishing Returns

subQuestions.questionText:
The schematic representation in the question paper shows a chromosome segment 'a b c d e' with a portion reversed in order, which causes chromosome mutation.
A. deletion
B. translocation
C. inversion
D. duplication
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - inversion (2 marks)
An inversion occurs when a chromosome segment breaks off, turns through 180° and re-attaches, so the order of the genes on that segment is reversed.

subQuestions.questionText:
A sheep has 27 pairs of chromosomes in the nucleus. The number of autosomes is …
A. 27.
B. 52.
C. 54.
D. 02.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - 52 (2 marks)
27 pairs = 54 chromosomes in total. One pair is the sex chromosomes, so the autosomes = 54 − 2 = 52 (26 pairs).

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a term from COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: Part of a business plan that provides an overall plan of action to promote sales.
COLUMN B options: A. management  B. bull  C. agri-demand chain  D. enterprise budget  E. marketing strategy  F. labour  G. controlled marketing  H. agri-marketing chain  I. whole farm budget  J. cow
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: E - marketing strategy (2 marks)
The marketing strategy section of a business plan sets out the overall plan of action for promoting and selling the product.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a term from COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: Stages of activity in the supply-demand chain from the point of production to consumption.
COLUMN B options: A. management  B. bull  C. agri-demand chain  D. enterprise budget  E. marketing strategy  F. labour  G. controlled marketing  H. agri-marketing chain  I. whole farm budget  J. cow
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: H - agri-marketing chain (2 marks)
The agri-marketing chain is the sequence of activities and role-players that move a product from producer to final consumer.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a term from COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: The document showing the amount of money the farmer thinks will be spent and earned on beef production.
COLUMN B options: A. management  B. bull  C. agri-demand chain  D. enterprise budget  E. marketing strategy  F. labour  G. controlled marketing  H. agri-marketing chain  I. whole farm budget  J. cow
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - enterprise budget (2 marks)
An enterprise budget estimates the expected income and expenditure of a single farm enterprise, such as beef production.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a term from COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: An effective combination and co-ordination of human, physical and financial resources to maximise profit.
COLUMN B options: A. management  B. bull  C. agri-demand chain  D. enterprise budget  E. marketing strategy  F. labour  G. controlled marketing  H. agri-marketing chain  I. whole farm budget  J. cow
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - management (2 marks)
Management is the process of combining and co-ordinating the resources of a business (people, physical assets and finance) to reach the goal of maximum profit.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a term from COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: The farm animal that determines the sex of a calf.
COLUMN B options: A. management  B. bull  C. agri-demand chain  D. enterprise budget  E. marketing strategy  F. labour  G. controlled marketing  H. agri-marketing chain  I. whole farm budget  J. cow
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - bull (2 marks)
The bull (male) contributes either an X or a Y sex chromosome in the sperm, so it determines the sex of the calf. The cow always contributes an X.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
A form of sustainable agricultural marketing that takes environmental concerns into consideration in production processes.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Green marketing (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
Money, manufactured goods and assets that can be used for production of other goods to generate income.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Capital (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
The type of selection whereby an individual is chosen based on records of its ancestors.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Pedigree (selection) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
An animal breeding system that often leads to the production of sterile offspring.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Species crossing (crossing of different species) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
The total number of gene effects that are inherited by the progeny that will determine their performance for breeding purposes.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Breeding value (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
Fresh produce marketing is a channel where a farmer sells the produce at the point of production.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Farm gate (marketing) (1 mark)
Selling at the point of production is farm-gate marketing. Fresh produce marketing takes place through fresh produce markets.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
Medium-term credit is the money borrowed from a financial institution to cover operational expenses.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Short-term (credit) (1 mark)
Money borrowed to cover day-to-day operational expenses, repayable within about one year, is short-term credit.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
Electroporation involves the use of fat carriers of the required DNA through the cell membrane into a nucleus.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Lipofection (1 mark)
Lipofection uses fat (lipid) carriers to transport DNA across the cell membrane. Electroporation uses an electric pulse to make the membrane permeable.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
Prepotency means that both alleles are equally dominant and visible in the phenotype of the offspring.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Co-dominance (1 mark)
Co-dominance is when both alleles are fully expressed in the phenotype. Prepotency is the ability of a parent to pass its characteristics strongly to its offspring.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
Multiple alleles refer to a large group of genes that each add to the value of certain phenotypic characteristics.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Polygenes (multiple genes) (1 mark)
Polygenes are many genes that each contribute a small additive effect to a quantitative characteristic. Multiple alleles are three or more alleles of the same gene.

questions.title: Section B, Question 2: Agricultural Management and Marketing

subQuestions.questionText:
An illustration in the question paper shows the different marketing functions of agricultural products, labelled A, B, C and D (A shows produce being moved by vehicle; D shows produce being converted/packed into a processed product).
Identify the marketing function illustrated by A and D.
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Transportation (1 mark)
D - Processing / value adding (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Marketing function B in the illustration is packaging. Name TWO guidelines for marketing function B (packaging).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Product identification / branding
• Must be recyclable / biodegradable
• Provide containment of the product
• Protect the product against damage
• Allow easy handling / convenience
• Warn of health risks
• Improve the shelf life of the product
• Be appropriate to the target market

subQuestions.questionText: Give THREE factors hampering the marketing of agricultural products.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any THREE (1 mark each):
• Poor infrastructure (roads, storage)
• Lack of capital
• Perishability of agricultural products
• Risks / accidents / theft / spoilage
• Ineffective control of production
• Seasonal fluctuations in production
• Wide distribution of the product and long distances to the market
• Low value in relation to volume
• Standardisation of products
• High marketing / intermediary / transport costs
• Legislation / strict marketing laws / export regulations

subQuestions.questionText:
A picture in the question paper shows a group of farmers meeting and discussing issues that will contribute towards their mutual economic and social needs.
Identify the type of marketing system represented by the farmers in the picture.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Co-operative marketing (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO principles of the marketing system identified in QUESTION 2.2.1 (co-operative marketing).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Voluntary and open membership
• Democratic member control
• Co-operation among members
• Members are provided with education, training and information
• Autonomy and independence
• Each member has a single vote
• Members contribute money equally
• Members are paid dividends
• Products are standardised
• Concern for the community
• Risk is shared by all members
• Only members may deliver products

subQuestions.label: 2.2.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Explain how the following will benefit the farmers in the co-operative marketing system:
(a) Members enjoy economies of scale in buying and selling.
subQuestions.memoText: Members of the co-operative save a lot of money by marketing as a group through a pool system; OR members buy inputs in bulk at cheaper prices, lowering the cost per unit. (2 marks)

subQuestions.label: 2.2.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText:
Explain how the following will benefit the farmers in the co-operative marketing system:
(b) Bargaining power.
subQuestions.memoText: Acting as one large group, the co-operative can negotiate better prices for inputs and for produce on behalf of all its members than any individual farmer could achieve alone. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows the supply and demand of oranges at different prices.
Price (R/kg) | Quantity demanded (kg) | Quantity supplied (kg)
6  | 1 400 | 200
8  | 1 200 | 400
10 | 1 000 | 600
12 | 800   | 800
14 | 600   | 1 000
16 | 400   | 1 200
18 | 200   | 1 400
Use the information in the table to draw a line graph representing both the supply and demand curves on the same set of axes.
subQuestions.memoText:
Line graph. Marking rubric (1 mark each):
• Correct heading
• X-axis correctly calibrated and labelled (Quantity demanded and supplied, kg)
• Y-axis correctly calibrated and labelled (Price, R)
• Correct units (R and kg)
• Line graph drawn (two lines: demand Qd sloping down, supply Qs sloping up)
• Accuracy of plotted points; the two lines intersect at price R12, quantity 800 kg
subQuestions.topic: Agricultural Marketing - Supply and Demand Graphs

subQuestions.label: 2.3.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the price in the table where there will be the largest shortage of oranges in the market.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: R6 (1 mark)
At R6 demand is 1 400 kg and supply is 200 kg, a shortage of 1 200 kg — the largest shortage.

subQuestions.label: 2.3.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the price in the table where there will be the lowest surplus of oranges in the market.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: R14 (1 mark)
At R14 supply is 1 000 kg and demand is 600 kg, a surplus of 400 kg — the smallest surplus among the prices where supply exceeds demand.

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the equilibrium price for oranges in the table above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: R12 (1 mark)
At R12 the quantity demanded (800 kg) equals the quantity supplied (800 kg), so the market is in equilibrium.

subQuestions.label: 2.4.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Two graphs (GRAPH A and GRAPH B) in the question paper illustrate the elasticity of supply and demand. GRAPH A shows a steep (near-vertical) curve; GRAPH B shows a flat (near-horizontal) curve.
Identify the graph (A or B) that represents price elasticity of supply.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Graph B (1 mark)
The flat curve shows that a small change in price causes a large change in quantity supplied — elastic supply.

subQuestions.label: 2.4.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the graph (A or B) that represents price inelasticity of demand.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Graph A (1 mark)
The steep curve shows that a large change in price causes only a small change in quantity demanded — inelastic demand.

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answers to QUESTION 2.4.1(a) and (b).
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) A small change in price resulted in a huge change in the quantity supplied. (1 mark)
(b) A huge change in price resulted in very little change in the quantity demanded. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO factors that affect demand.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Availability of substitute products
• Price of complementary and competing products
• Research
• Fashion
• Quality of the product
• Consumer preferences / tastes
• Festive seasons
• Usefulness of the product
• Number of consumers
• Legislation
• Advertising of the product
• Price of the product / price expectations
• Income / buying power / socio-economic circumstances of consumers

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the scenario: A young successful livestock farmer started farming in a dry region of South Africa. After receiving a young heifer as a gift, the heifer gave birth to a calf which was raised and sold at a good price. With that money the farmer bought five calves. The young farmer now owns 18 cows and 1 790 hectares of land, employs four permanent farm workers, and the cows' calving rate is 98%.
The young livestock farmer qualifies to be an entrepreneur. Justify this statement.
subQuestions.memoText: The young farmer took the initiative to organise a farming business from the gift, accepting its risks in order to make a profit. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Deduce TWO entrepreneurial success factors for the farmer from the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Initiative / creativity / innovation
• Confidence
• Perseverance
• Market driven
• Communication / interpersonal skills
• Vision
• Hard-working / commitment
• Courage / motivation / positive attitude
• Risk taking
• Achievement orientation
• Knowledge / skills

subQuestions.label: 2.5.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify TWO strengths of the farming business in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• The farmer possesses many entrepreneurial success factors
• Owns 1 790 hectares of land
• Achieved a 98% calving rate
• Has permanent workers
• The farmer is young and energetic

subQuestions.label: 2.5.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify ONE threat to the business in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText: Farming in a dry / arid region (risk of drought and feed shortage). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.1.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
A graph in the question paper shows the hectares of land available for cultivation (arable land) and for human settlement for a small community over the years 1970 to 2020. Arable land falls steadily from about 70 ha in 1970 to about 10 ha in 2020, while land for human settlement rises over the same period.
Deduce an economic characteristic of land depicted by the graph.
subQuestions.memoText: The availability of land is limited (land is fixed in supply). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.1.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Deduce a function of land as a production factor from the graph above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Land provides space (for settlement / cultivation)
• Land provides food

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 3.1.1(a).
subQuestions.memoText: Arable land was about 70 hectares in 1970 and decreased over the years to only about 10 hectares in 2020, yet no new land could be created — it is limited. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO functions of land not reflected in the graph above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Land is a source of raw materials
• Land is a source of minerals
• Land is an asset / serves as collateral (security for loans)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate TWO methods farmers can apply to improve land productivity as from the year 2020 to ensure a constant supply of food.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Improve soil fertility (fertilisers, crop rotation)
• Improve water management / water supply (irrigation)
• Restore land potential (reclaim degraded land)
• Change cropping practices and farming systems
• Farm the land more efficiently / precision farming
• Consolidate small uneconomical land units

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the scenario: The agricultural sector was hard hit by the Covid-19 pandemic. The virus affected mostly the older, experienced labourers, resulting in their deaths. Farmers had to rely on inexperienced workers for tasks such as fencing and harvesting.
Identify, from the scenario, the TWO main types of labourers employed on a farm based on the period of employment.
subQuestions.memoText:
• Permanent / full-time labourers (1 mark)
• Temporary / part-time labourers (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.2.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify, in the scenario above, the task that is done by casual labourers.
subQuestions.memoText: Fencing (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.2.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify, in the scenario above, the task that is done by seasonal labourers.
subQuestions.memoText: Harvesting (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the labour problem in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Lack of skills / training
• Scarcity of labour
• Loss of experienced workers due to Covid-19

subQuestions.questionText: Name the method that farmers can put in place to address the problem identified in QUESTION 3.2.3.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Train labourers / employ skilled labour
• Employ additional workers / improve working conditions
• Vaccination / enforce Covid-19 protocols

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows the conditions of employment on FARM A and FARM B.
Condition | Farm A labourer | Farm B labourer
Rate/day (R) | 120 | 200
Normal working hours/week | 52 | 40
Leave days/year | 14 | 30
Overtime payment | R35/hour | R50/hour
Identify, in the table above, the employee whose conditions of employment are unfair.
subQuestions.memoText: Farm A labourer (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons to support the answer to QUESTION 3.3.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each), comparing Farm A with Farm B:
• Lower rate per day (R120 vs R200)
• Longer normal working hours per week (52 vs 40)
• Fewer leave days per year (14 vs 30)
• Lower overtime payment (R35/hour vs R50/hour)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the labour legislation that the employer has violated.
subQuestions.memoText: Basic Conditions of Employment Act / BCEA (Act No. 75 of 1997) (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.4.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows the value of capital items in a farming enterprise over five years.
Year | Capital item A (R) | Capital item B (R)
2016 | 350 000 | 1 200 000
2017 | 280 000 | 1 250 000
2018 | 250 000 | 1 300 000
2019 | 150 000 | 1 400 000
2020 | 90 000 | 1 500 000
Identify the capital item representing fixed capital.
subQuestions.memoText:
Capital item B (1 mark)
Its value increases over time, which is typical of fixed capital such as land and buildings.

subQuestions.label: 3.4.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the capital item representing movable capital.
subQuestions.memoText:
Capital item A (1 mark)
Its value decreases over time (depreciation), which is typical of movable capital such as machinery and vehicles.

subQuestions.questionText: Give an example of each capital item in QUESTION 3.4.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
• Fixed capital (item B): land / farm / building / borehole / fence (1 mark)
• Movable capital (item A): tractor / truck / machinery / livestock (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Deduce the problem of capital as reflected by capital item A in the table above.
subQuestions.memoText: Depreciation (loss of value over time). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows a financial record for the first quarter of the year.
Item | January (R) | February (R) | March (R)
Opening balance | 2 500 | 18 372 | 29 472
Receipts: cash sales on crops | 15 322 | 9 500 | 2 800
Receipts: rental | 10 000 | 10 000 | 10 000
Total receipts | 25 322 | 19 500 | 12 800
Payments: salaries/wages | 6 000 | 4 900 | 3 200
Payments: seeds and fuel | 3 450 | 3 500 | 1 100
Total payments | 9 450 | 8 400 | 4 300
Closing balance | 18 372 | 29 472 | 37 972
Identify the financial record shown in the table above.
subQuestions.memoText: Cash flow statement (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason to support the answer to QUESTION 3.5.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): it reflects an opening balance / a closing balance / receipts (income) / payments (expenditure) for each month.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the total amount available to run the enterprise at the beginning of the second quarter.
subQuestions.memoText: R37 972 (the closing balance for March). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the total costs over the first quarter.
subQuestions.memoText:
Total costs = total payments for January + February + March
= R9 450 + R8 400 + R4 300
= R22 150 (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the management skill that will enable the manager to do the following:
(a) Dealing with labour problems
(b) Avoiding financial losses on the farm
(c) Allocating labourers and available resources appropriately
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Problem-solving / interpersonal skill (1 mark)
(b) Financial management skill (1 mark)
(c) Organisation and co-ordination skill (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.7.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
A farming business is coupled with risk factors. Indicate the risk management strategy applicable to the following situation:
(a) The farmer joins a co-operative where they produce and market as a collective.
subQuestions.memoText: Risk sharing (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.7.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate the risk management strategy applicable to the following situation:
(b) The farmer keeps livestock, grows crops and is also involved in agritourism activities.
subQuestions.memoText: Diversification (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name THREE factors that are beyond the direct control of the farmer which can affect the farming business.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any THREE (1 mark each):
• Economic forces
• Political forces
• Ethical forces
• Legal forces
• Socio-cultural forces
• Competitive forces
• Technological forces
• Environmental forces

questions.title: Section B, Question 4: Basic Agricultural Genetics

subQuestions.questionText:
Gregor Mendel was the first person to study how the characteristics of pea plants are transferred from parents to offspring.
Name the term that refers to the study in the statement above.
subQuestions.memoText: Genetics (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO of Mendel's laws of inheritance.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• The law of dominance
• The law of segregation
• The law of independent assortment (recombination)

subQuestions.questionText:
Feather colour in chickens is controlled by two pairs of genes:
• Colour gene — alleles B = black and b = white
• Epistatic gene — alleles L = no colour and l = with colour
Complete the table by giving the phenotype for genotype BBLl.
subQuestions.memoText:
White (1 mark)
The dominant epistatic allele L masks the colour gene, so any bird with at least one L is white regardless of the B/b alleles.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the phenotype for genotype Bbll (colour gene B = black, b = white; epistatic gene L = no colour, l = with colour).
subQuestions.memoText:
Black (1 mark)
With the recessive epistatic genotype ll the colour gene is expressed, and the dominant B allele produces black.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the phenotype for genotype bbll (colour gene B = black, b = white; epistatic gene L = no colour, l = with colour).
subQuestions.memoText:
White (1 mark)
With genotype ll the colour gene is expressed, and the homozygous recessive bb produces white.

subQuestions.questionText:
A diagram in the question paper shows a cross between parents where (Bb) represents a farm animal with horns and (bb) a farm animal with no horns (polled). The Punnett square gives the offspring BB, Bb, Bb, bb.
Identify a phenotype visible in the offspring.
subQuestions.memoText:
Horned OR polled (no horns) (1 mark)
The offspring BB and Bb are horned; bb is polled.

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the percentage of offspring with the homozygous recessive phenotype (from the cross producing BB, Bb, Bb, bb).
subQuestions.memoText:
1 out of 4 offspring is bb (homozygous recessive).
= 1/4 × 100
= 25% (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
A dominant homozygous boar was mated with a heterozygous sow. In the F1-generation all the offspring were red. (In the F2-generation a genetically unknown boar was mated with a heterozygous F1 sow, resulting in half the offspring being white.)
Use the letters R for red and r for white to draw a Punnett square and determine the ratio of the genotypes in the first crossing (RR × Rr).
subQuestions.memoText:
Cross: RR (boar) × Rr (sow).
Male gametes: R and R. Female gametes: R and r.
Punnett square offspring: RR, Rr, RR, Rr.
Marking (1 mark each):
• Correct male gametes (R, R)
• Correct female gametes (R, r)
• Correct offspring (RR, Rr, RR, Rr)
• Punnett square correctly populated with gametes and offspring
• Genotypic ratio = 2 RR : 2 Rr (i.e. 1 RR : 1 Rr)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate, from the information above, the genotype of the genetically unknown boar used in the F2-generation (mated with a heterozygous Rr sow, producing half white offspring).
subQuestions.memoText:
rr (homozygous recessive / white). (1 mark)
Rr × rr gives 1/2 Rr (red) : 1/2 rr (white).

subQuestions.label: 4.5.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
In a breeding programme two green pepper cultivars were crossed to produce offspring for a specific purpose.
Give the genetic term for: a drastic improvement in the yield of the offspring was achieved.
subQuestions.memoText: Heterosis / hybrid vigour (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.5.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Give the genetic term for: the two individual cultivars were picked based on the records of their respective offspring.
subQuestions.memoText: Progeny selection (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.5.1(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Give the genetic term for: measuring the biological characteristics by using computer technology.
subQuestions.memoText: Biometrics (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why the two cultivars above were used in the breeding programme.
subQuestions.memoText: They were superior parents with the desired characteristics, so they can produce offspring with the required / superior characteristics. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below indicates the heritability (%) of different hereditary traits for sheep.
Characteristic | Heritability (%)
Birth weight | 53
Post-weaning gain | 60
Lean meat | 37
Fleece weight | 57
Identify the characteristic with the lowest improvement in the breeding programme.
subQuestions.memoText: Lean meat (heritability 37%, the lowest, so it responds least to selection). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.6.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the heritability table above. Indicate the hereditary characteristic that should be focused on for the most effective improvement for a farmer having a feedlot.
subQuestions.memoText:
Post-weaning gain (1 mark)
A feedlot fattens animals after weaning, so growth rate after weaning is the priority trait.

subQuestions.label: 4.6.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the hereditary characteristic that should be focused on for the most effective improvement for a stud farmer supplying pure-bred animals to other commercial mutton farmers to be used for breeding.
subQuestions.memoText:
Birth weight (1 mark)
Birth weight influences survival, ease of birth and later growth of the breeding animals supplied.

subQuestions.label: 4.6.2(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the hereditary characteristic that should be focused on for the most effective improvement for a wool farmer.
subQuestions.memoText: Fleece weight (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE other factor (besides heredity) to improve the post-weaning gain (production output) in a flock of sheep.
subQuestions.memoText: Environmental / external factors (e.g. nutrition, feeding, health / parasite control, management). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
CROSSINGS A, B and C represent different breeding systems used in cattle production:
A: Holstein stud bull × breeding of inferior cows, with repeated breeding back to their offspring.
B: Hereford bull × Hereford cow (the bull's own daughter).
C: Afrikaner bull × Shorthorn cow.
Identify the breeding systems represented by CROSSINGS A, B and C.
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Upgrading (grading up) (1 mark)
B - Inbreeding (1 mark)
C - Crossbreeding (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO disadvantages of the breeding system represented by CROSSING B (inbreeding).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Loss of genetic variation / diversity
• Leads to inbreeding depression (reduced production / fertility)
• Increased expression of lethal genes
• Expensive system
• Reduced vitality
• Homozygosity of unwanted genes / deformities

subQuestions.questionText:
A picture in the question paper shows a technique in which a fine glass needle is used to inject genetic material directly into the nucleus of a cell held by a pipette.
Identify the technique used to genetically modify organisms.
subQuestions.memoText: Micro-injection (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Differentiate between conventional hybrid cultivars and GMOs.
subQuestions.memoText:
• Conventional hybrid: the DNA is not altered; it is produced by crossing two lines / cultivars of the same species. (1 mark)
• GMO: the DNA is altered; genes from another organism are inserted into the cell. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO potential risks associated with genetically modified plants.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Health risks / allergies
• Environmental risks (e.g. gene flow to wild relatives, loss of biodiversity)
• Economic / financial risks (dependence on seed companies)
